1.why: Screens use a clean sans-serif with comfortable line spacing, and the setup key and recovery codes are rendered in letter-spaced monospace, although the tiny provisioning URL is cramped.

2.why: No italics or all-caps prose is used, but the small-type otpauth 'Provisioning details' URL is a dense unbroken block of text on the setup screen.

3.why: The single-column card layout with large type and wrapping text is simple enough to remain readable and well laid out at phone width.

4.why: Guidance is mostly short plain sentences such as 'Store these now. They will not be shown again.', with jargon limited to 'TOTP SHA-256' and the provisioning URI.

5.why: The recovery-code field shows an 'ABCD-EFGH-JKLM' placeholder example, but the six-digit verification-code field shows no example of the expected input.

6.why: No screen forces the user to read a long block of text; the most text anywhere is a couple of short sentences plus the code list.

7.why: The setup key and recovery codes are shown only as plain text with no copy button, download, or print affordance, so the user must transcribe them by hand.

8.why: The authenticator setup screen offers no QR code, only a manual key and a raw otpauth URL that would still have to be entered manually.

9.why: The conventional email/password form should work with password managers, but nothing observed indicates one-time-code autofill support for the OTP or recovery-code fields.

10.why: Each screen has a single bold heading naming the step and a solid-blue primary button that clearly outweighs the grey and red secondary buttons.

11.why: Every step asks for one task at a time (sign in, verify, save codes) with Back/Cancel clearly secondary, although the settings hub does present three choices.

12.why: Banners such as 'MFA is active.', 'Recovery code accepted. 7 recovery codes remain.' and 'Your secure session has been invalidated.' plainly state what happened and what comes next, even though the accepted message is oddly styled red.

13.why: Steps can be retried and a new setup key generated, but five failures lock verification for five minutes (a penalty) and there are no reveal/hide or resend-code controls.

14.why: The observed error 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.' avoids blaming the user but does not state what the problem was or how to fix it.

15.why: Reading has no timer, but codes expire every 30 seconds and a five-minute lockout follows repeated failures, so entry time is limited rather than generous.
